input.series: the spread, the ordinary level and the scale of (s3) (spread_mr_fhs's MAD of 20 daily changes, floor 0.5), all as (s3) reads them, and the calendar flags of the target day. No new panel column is read.
input.one_step_residual: z1(j) = ((spread[j] - level[j-1]) - phi * (spread[j-1] - level[j-1])) / scale[j-1] - shift(flags of row j), with phi the base fit's and shift the lead-1 calendar terms of (s3) (spread_mr_state_calendar.standardised_shift). It reads rows j and j-1, the level and scale of row j-1 and the flags of row j itself (direct, never one row off). It is None where there is no level or scale.
input.own_band: (s3)'s own 90% band, in these units: the 5th and 95th percentile (protocol_benchmarks.empirical_quantiles) of z1 over the refit's training window, rows from five rows plus the decision lag before the window start up to the anchor. A row is a miss when z1 is strictly outside it. The band is fitted at each refit and held until the next; a row after the refit is judged against it (the band is known at the refit, not after). READING SETTLED HERE, not by Eleonora: the issue says 'the spread printed outside (s3)'s own 90% band'; (s3) forecasts at k = h + lag steps, and the band here is its one-step version, so a miss is the day's own surprise and not the k-step interval. See the pull request's marked question 1.
input.availability: every row read is at or before the anchor, the last row whose spread is public at the decision (protocol_benchmarks._require_public raises LookAheadError); a miss, an episode flag or a filtered probability of a row the track has not read raises LookAheadError (Track._require_read)
input.missing: a row with no level or no scale has no residual: it is no miss, and the filter only moves the chain on

arms.principle: Filtered historical simulation stays and the base is (s3): forecast = centre + scale(anchor) * (shift + z_h), with shift the fitted calendar terms in standardised units and z_h the quantiles of the pool of the standardised residuals after the terms. An arm changes which pool, and for the Markov arms what scale multiplier, the law takes; the terms, the centre, phi, the refit cadence (21 rows) and the training pairs are (s3)'s.

listed_in_full.m1_episode_k3: (m1) observable episode state, memory k = 3: an origin or the anchor is in an episode when a miss fell on any of the 3 rows ending at it. In an episode the law takes the pool (and with it the scale, which is the spread of that pool in standardised units) of the training pairs whose origin was in an episode; outside, the pool of the calm origins; with fewer than 60 origins in the state, (s3)'s full pool. The terms are (s3)'s, fitted on all pairs: READING SETTLED HERE, the issue says 'the residual pool and scale come from past in-episode origins only'; there is no separate scale multiplier, the pool's own spread is the scale. See the pull request's marked question 2.
listed_in_full.m2_markov: (m2) two-state Markov-switching scale. z1 is N(0, sigma_s^2) in a calm (0) or stress (1) state; the state is a Markov chain with entry probability p01 (constant) and stay probability p11. Fitted by EM (forward-backward, scaled) on the z1 of the training window, state 1 starting as the high-scale state (starting scales 0.6 and 1.8 times the rms, entry 0.05, stay 0.90, at most 60 iterations, stop when the log-likelihood moves by less than 1e-6); a fit whose stress scale is below 1.05 times the calm scale, or a window with fewer than 120 residuals, is degenerate (one scale) and is (s3). The state probability at a row is the Hamilton filter over the z1 up to and including that row, started at the chain's stationary share. The k-step predictive probability of stress from a row is the filter propagated k steps. (s3)'s residuals e of lead h (k = h + lag steps apart) are divided by sqrt((1-pi) sigma_0^2 + pi sigma_1^2), pi the k-step stress probability from their own origin; the forecast is the mixture, weighted by the k-step stress probability from the anchor, of that pool scaled by sigma_0 and by sigma_1, its distribution function the weighted sum of the two scaled continuous laws whose quantile functions interpolate the pool, inverted by bisection.
listed_in_full.m3_markov_calendar: (m3) (m2) with the entry probability p01 = logistic(a + b . x), x the 0/1 flags of the day entered: month_end (the turn), quarter_end (the quarter-end turn), tax_date and settlement_coupon (the coupon settlement), read at that day itself. Fitted by EM with a Newton step on the soft-count logistic likelihood, an L2 penalty of 1 on the slopes. A scheduled flag (the coupon settlement) is public at the decision of the business day before it (asof rule 2), so a step to a day beyond the day after the decision reads it as 0; the calendar columns are known whenever read. The h-step probability propagates step by step, each step with its own day's flags. READING SETTLED HERE: the issue's 'turn, quarter-end turn, tax date, coupon settlement' are mapped to the four terms of spread_mr_calendar named above, and the flags of the days between the anchor and the target are read as calendar dates. See the pull request's marked question 3.

scoring.hit_rules: OPEN QUESTION, Eleonora's (#993): whole-bp outcomes tie with a quantile. The strict ('above') and at-or-beyond ('at_or_above') rules and the randomised tie rule of #1156 ('randomised') are reported side by side; none is chosen. The randomised rule is run with coverage_tests.randomised_hit_sequence and tie_hit_probability: the forecast is 23 quantiles of a continuous law, linear between them, so P(Y < q) = P(Y <= q) = the level at every quantile and the tie probability is 0; the rule then coincides with 'above' and the page says so. The draws are seeded with 1182 and recorded. Upper exceedance: y > q ('above') or y >= q ('at_or_above'). Lower exceedance: y < q or y <= q, the mirror. A band is missed when the outcome is outside it, so under 'above' the band is closed and under 'at_or_above' it is open
scoring.runs: a run is a maximal block of consecutive hits in the per-lead sequence of consecutive decision days. Mean run length = hits / runs; longest = the longest block. Under independence at a 10% miss rate the mean run is about 1.11

kill_rule.text: The issue's: if no arm moves independence off p = 0.000 at any lead, and no arm cuts the mean run by more than 15%, state that the clustering is not a two-state phenomenon either, and recommend reporting it as a known limit in the use limitation rather than another arm.
kill_rule.reading: 'off 0.000' is a p-value of at least 0.0005 for the Christoffersen independence test of the 90% band's misses, pooled, at any of the five leads, under any of the three hit rules. 'cuts the mean run by more than 15%' is a mean run of the 90% band (closed rule, pooled over leads) below 0.85 times (s3)'s. The page lists, for every arm, the leads off 0.000 under each rule, the mean and longest run and the cut against (s3)'s, and says whether the kill rule is met. It states the recommendation if so; adopting it is Eleonora's decision

adoption: The issue's: an arm replaces (s3) only if independence is no longer rejected at the leads, or the mean miss run falls clearly towards 1.1, without losing CRPS beyond the interval. That is her decision on the page. The page lists the facts (leads off 0.000, the mean run and its cut, the pooled grid CRPS reading against (s3) on the mean-d bound and the regimes and day types read as a loss) and settles nothing.

rules: An arm's gain over (s3) is read as present on a split when the studentized one-sided bound on mean(d) of its grid CRPS excludes zero on the positive side (the two-sided 90% interval of mean(d) is above zero), and as a loss when that interval is below zero; otherwise undecided. The skill interval is shown beside and not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime and pressure-day-type splits beside it; a gain pooled and a loss in 2018-19, 2021-23 or on quarter-end days is reported as mixed.

A calibration measure moving toward its nominal value is reported with its interval; a hit-sequence p-value is reported as a p-value and is no gate. Run lengths are reported as counts with no interval.
Nothing in this study is a verdict, and the page says so.
